10. SP5X EXECUTION METHOD
======================================================================

The mission itself MUST use five materially distinct recursive passes.

This is not "review five times."

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 1 — RECONSTRUCT + CONTRACT

Do not implement broad fixes until this exists.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 2 — BREAK + ADVERSARIAL HARDENING
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Attack both existing architecture AND the proposed repair.

- false transaction assumptions
- stranded states
- replay hazards
- duplicated side effects
- stale approvals
- lease forgery/reuse

- idempotency collisions
- artifact identity collisions
- partial writes
- dirty-repo edge cases
- symlink/path issues
- driver output trust escalation
- private/public authority leakage
- model/prompt privilege escalation
- restart after every meaningful stage

Use discriminating tests, not commentary.

Every real finding must become:
    invariant
    regression
    correction
or
    documented accepted limitation

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 3 — WHAT'S LEFT + CHECKPOINT COMPLETION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

After the repairs:

    WHAT STILL PREVENTS THE APPROVED v0.7 CHECKPOINT FROM BEING TRUE?

- unintegrated existing work
- unproven implementation
- missing acceptance tests
- missing operator surfaces
- missing persistence/restart proof
- cross-repo coupling
- branch divergence
- dead code
- stale docs
- missing package exports
- clean-install gaps
- provider/model proof gaps
- security proof gaps
- incomplete evidence boundaries

Do not add requirements invented during this pass.

Only finish what the checkpoint actually requires.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 4 — INVERT + MINIMIZE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Assume the repair/implementation plan has become too large.

Challenge every new abstraction.

Ask:

- Can Core's existing primitive handle this?
- Are we duplicating EventStore semantics?
- Are we adding a second lifecycle?
- Are we moving private concepts into public Core unnecessarily?
- Is a projection fix sufficient?
- Can a state transition reuse an existing contract?
- Is migration avoidable?
- Is backwards compatibility preserved?
- Can fewer changes satisfy more invariants?

Also assume the approved checkpoint itself is being misread.

Try to falsify the claimed boundary using:
- commit history
- DecisionRecords
- acceptance evidence
- docs
- current tests

Shrink the implementation to the smallest architecture that actually satisfies
the approved checkpoint.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 5 — SYNTHESIZE + RELEASE-GRADE CLOSURE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Integrate the strongest surviving result.

Then verify from clean state.

Required closure layers:

A. TARGETED TESTS
All changed subsystems.

B. ADVERSARIAL TESTS
Every security/lifecycle invariant added.

C. CANONICAL TRACKED SUITE
Use the tracked test boundary.

Do not allow local untracked scratch scripts to pollute pytest discovery.

If relevant, canonical invocation should target:

    tests/

rather than arbitrary local root discovery.

D. CONTRACT / CONFORMANCE GATES
Run existing CAPT conformance gates.

E. PACKAGE BUILD
Build distributable artifact.

F. CLEAN INSTALL
Verify imports/CLI from clean install without source-tree leakage.

G. NORMAL OPERATOR ACCEPTANCE
Exercise CAPT through its real operator architecture.

H. RESTART ACCEPTANCE
Checkpoint → stop/process loss → restore → inspect state → continue safely.

I. REAL GOVERNED DRIVER ACCEPTANCE
Where approved/provider credentials permit it.

J. DOCUMENTATION TRUTH AUDIT
Every claim must match current proof.

======================================================================

======================================================================

Use precise classifications:

MISSING

IMPLEMENTED
Code exists.

UNIT_PROVEN
Unit behavior tested.

INTEGRATION_PROVEN
Subsystem boundaries tested.

RESTART_PROVEN
Correct restore/replay behavior demonstrated.

OPERATOR_PROVEN
Normal CLI/UI architecture exercised.

REAL_MODEL_PROVEN
Actual governed provider/model path exercised.

PRIVATE_ONLY

DEFERRED

BLOCKED
Cannot complete because of a concrete external dependency.

into:

    implementation exists

into:

======================================================================

Before modifying:

- identify branch
- identify HEAD
- identify remote
- identify pre-existing dirt
- identify user-owned untracked files

Do NOT destroy or overwrite unrelated operator work.

Do not rewrite unrelated history.

Do not push/merge unless authority exists.

If an existing PR/branch corresponds to the approved v0.7 work:

======================================================================
13. CROSS-REPO DISCIPLINE
======================================================================

CAPT Core is public authority.

capt-private may contain useful advanced implementations.

Treasure chest may contain historical gold.

Do not solve public architecture by accidentally making it depend on private
runtime authority.

If useful private implementation should be ported:

1. identify exact source
2. identify dependencies
3. identify authority assumptions
4. identify algorithmic/core value
5. port only compatible behavior
6. remove private authority coupling
7. test in public Core independently

Record:

    REUSED
    ADAPTED
    REWRITTEN
    REJECTED

with rationale.

======================================================================
14. STOP CONDITIONS
======================================================================

STOP when ALL of the following are true:

1. Ouroboros defects confirmed by source are repaired.
2. Corresponding regressions pass.
3. Failure finalization cannot produce stranded state for tested paths.
4. Negative verification is authoritative/persistent.

16. FINAL QUALITY GATE
======================================================================

Before declaring closure, perform one final SP5 synthesis over the completed
state.

If any answer exposes a material unresolved defect inside the approved
checkpoint:

DO NOT CLAIM CLOSURE.

Repair it or classify the checkpoint blocked.

FINAL STANDARD:

    FIX THE DRAGON'S LANDING GEAR.

10. SP5X EXECUTION METHOD
======================================================================

The mission itself MUST use five materially distinct recursive passes.

This is not "review five times."

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 1 — RECONSTRUCT + CONTRACT

Do not implement broad fixes until this exists.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 2 — BREAK + ADVERSARIAL HARDENING
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Attack both existing architecture AND the proposed repair.

- false transaction assumptions
- stranded states
- replay hazards
- duplicated side effects
- stale approvals
- lease forgery/reuse
- maxUses inconsistencies
- evidence/verification conflation

- operator semantic ambiguity

- idempotency collisions
- artifact identity collisions
- partial writes
- dirty-repo edge cases

    correction
or

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 3 — WHAT'S LEFT + CHECKPOINT COMPLETION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

- missing persistence/restart proof
- cross-repo coupling
- branch divergence
- dead code
- stale docs
- missing package exports
- clean-install gaps
- provider/model proof gaps
- security proof gaps
- incomplete evidence boundaries

Do not add requirements invented during this pass.

Only finish what the checkpoint actually requires.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PASS 4 — INVERT + MINIMIZE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Assume the repair/implementation plan has become too large.

Challenge every new abstraction.

- Can Core's existing primitive handle this?
- Are we duplicating EventStore semantics?
- Are we adding a second lifecycle?
- Are we moving private concepts into public Core unnecessarily?
- Is a projection fix sufficient?
- Can a state transition reuse an existing contract?
- Is migration avoidable?

- DecisionRecords
- acceptance evidence
- docs
- current tests

the approved checkpoint.

PASS 5 — SYNTHESIZE + RELEASE-GRADE CLOSURE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Integrate the strongest surviving result.

Then verify from clean state.

Required closure layers:

A. TARGETED TESTS
All changed subsystems.

B. ADVERSARIAL TESTS
Every security/lifecycle invariant added.

C. CANONICAL TRACKED SUITE
Use the tracked test boundary.

Do not allow local untracked scratch scripts to pollute pytest discovery.

If relevant, canonical invocation should target:

    tests/

rather than arbitrary local root discovery.

D. CONTRACT / CONFORMANCE GATES
Run existing CAPT conformance gates.

E. PACKAGE BUILD
Build distributable artifact.

F. CLEAN INSTALL
Verify imports/CLI from clean install without source-tree leakage.

G. NORMAL OPERATOR ACCEPTANCE
Exercise CAPT through its real operator architecture.

H. RESTART ACCEPTANCE
Checkpoint → stop/process loss → restore → inspect state → continue safely.

I. REAL GOVERNED DRIVER ACCEPTANCE
Where approved/provider credentials permit it.

J. DOCUMENTATION TRUTH AUDIT
Every claim must match current proof.

======================================================================

Use precise classifications:

MISSING
No implementation.

IMPLEMENTED
Code exists.

UNIT_PROVEN
Unit behavior tested.

INTEGRATION_PROVEN
Subsystem boundaries tested.

RESTART_PROVEN
Correct restore/replay behavior demonstrated.

OPERATOR_PROVEN
Normal CLI/UI architecture exercised.

REAL_MODEL_PROVEN
Actual governed provider/model path exercised.

ACCEPTANCE_PROVEN
Approved end-to-end checkpoint path demonstrated.

EXPERIMENTAL
Implemented but insufficiently measured/proven.

PRIVATE_ONLY
Not part of public Core.

DEFERRED
Explicitly beyond checkpoint.

BLOCKED
Cannot complete because of a concrete external dependency.

Do not turn:

    tests pass

into:

    production ready.

Do not turn:

    implementation exists

into:

    checkpoint complete.

Record:

with rationale.

{"content": "1|\"\"\"Typed errors for the CAPT runtime.\n2|\n3|Each maps to an ErrorEnvelope category in the contract set. Distinct classes\n4|exist so tests can assert the *reason* a write was refused, not merely that\n5|it was refused.\n6|\"\"\"\n7|\n8|from __future__ import annotations\n9|\n10|from typing import List, Optional\n11|\n12|\n13|class CaptRuntimeError(Exception):\n14|    \"\"\"Base class. Carries the contract error category.\"\"\"\n15|\n16|    category = \"internal\"\n17|\n18|\n19|class ContractViolation(CaptRuntimeError):\n20|    \"\"\"A payload failed generated-contract validation.\"\"\"\n21|\n22|    category = \"validation\"\n23|\n24|    def __init__(self, type_name: str, errors: List[str]) -> None:\n25|        CaptRuntimeError.__init__(self, \"%s: %s\" % (type_name, \"; \".join(errors)))\n26|        self.type_name = type_name\n27|        self.errors = errors\n28|\n29|\n30|class AuthorityViolation(CaptRuntimeError):\n31|    \"\"\"An actor attempted an action reserved to another authority plane.\"\"\"\n32|\n33|    category = \"authority\"\n34|\n35|\n36|class ConcurrencyConflict(CaptRuntimeError):\n37|    \"\"\"Expected aggregate version did not match the stored version.\"\"\"\n38|\n39|    category = \"concurrency\"\n40|\n41|    def __init__(self, stream_id: str, expected: int, actual: int) -> None:\n42|        CaptRuntimeError.__init__(\n43|            self,\n44|            \"stale write to %s: expected version %d, actual %d\"\n45|            % (stream_id, expected, actual),\n46|        )\n47|        self.stream_id = stream_id\n48|        self.expected = expected\n49|        self.actual = actual\n50|\n51|\n52|class IdempotencyConflict(CaptRuntimeError):\n53|    \"\"\"An idempotency key was reused with a different operation fingerprint.\"\"\"\n54|\n55|    category = \"idempotency\"\n56|\n57|\n58|class IntegrityViolation(CaptRuntimeError):\n59|    \"\"\"A digest check failed: ledger, payload, or checkpoint.\"\"\"\n60|\n61|    category = \"integrity\"\n62|\n63|\n64|class NotFound(CaptRuntimeError):\n65|    category = \"not_found\"\n66|\n67|\n68|class IllegalTransition(CaptRuntimeError):\n69|    \"\"\"A state machine rejected a transition.\"\"\"\n70|\n71|    category = \"illegal_transition\"\n72|\n73|    def __init__(self, subject: str, from_state: str, to_state: str) -> None:\n74|     self.lease_id = lease_id\n91|\n92|\n93|class CapabilityViolation(CaptRuntimeError):\n94|    \"\"\"A read-only capability-model invariant was violated (M0-B).\"\"\"\n95|\n96|    category = {"content": "1|\"\"\"Authority planes and the structural separation between them.\n2|\n3|Spec invariants 1-5 require that governance, cognition, execution,\n4|verification, and claim authority remain distinct. Encoding the rules here —\n5|rather than as review guidance — is what makes them testable.\n6|\"\"\"\n7|\n8|from __future__ import annotations\n9|\n10|from typing import Dict, FrozenSet\n11|\n12|from .errors import AuthorityViolation\n13|\n14|GOVERNANCE = \"governance_kernel\"\n15|COGNITION = \"cognitive_plane\"\n16|EXECUTION = \"execution_plane\"\n17|VERIFICATION = \"verification_plane\"\n18|CLAIM_AUTHORITY = \"claim_authority\"\n19|HUMAN = \"human\"\n20|SYSTEM = \"system\"\n21|EXTERNAL_DRIVER = \"external_driver\"\n22|\n23|# Which actor kinds may author which authoritative act. Deny by default:\n24|# an act not listed here has no permitted author at all.\n25|_PERMITTED: Dict[str, FrozenSet[str]] = {\n26|    \"evaluate_policy\": frozenset({GOVERNANCE}),\n27|    \"issue_grant\": frozenset({GOVERNANCE}),\n28|    \"revoke\": frozenset({GOVERNANCE, HUMAN}),\n29|    \"activate_lease\": frozenset({GOVERNANCE}),\n30|    \"reserve_use\": frozenset({EXECUTION}),\n31|    \"finalize_use\": frozenset({EXECUTION}),\n32|    \"create_mission\": frozenset({HUMAN, SYSTEM}),\n33|    \"plan_tasks\": frozenset({COGNITION, SYSTEM}),\n34|    \"transition_task\": frozenset({EXECUTION, SYSTEM}),\n35|    \"submit_result\": frozenset({EXECUTION, SYSTEM}),\n36|    \"request_human_approval\": frozenset({EXECUTION, GOVERNANCE, SYSTEM}),\n37|    \"submit_human_approval_decision\": frozenset({HUMAN}),\n38|    \"cancel_task\": frozenset({EXECUTION, HUMAN, SYSTEM}),\n39|    \"cancel_driver_run\": frozenset({EXECUTION, HUMAN, SYSTEM}),\n40|    \"record_evidence\": frozenset({VERIFICATION, EXECUTION, SYSTEM}),\n41|    \"produce_verification\": frozenset({VERIFICATION}),\n42|    \"propose_claim\": frozenset({COGNITION, EXECUTION, SYSTEM}),\n43|    \"decide_claim\": frozenset({CLAIM_AUTHORITY}),\n44|    \"create_checkpoint\": frozenset({SYSTEM}),\n45|}\n46|\n47|\n48|def permitted_actors(act: str) -> FrozenSet[str]:\n49|    return _PERMITTED.get(act, frozenset())\n50|\n51|\n52|def require_authority(act: str, actor_kind: str) -> None:\n53|    \"\"\"Raise AuthorityViolation unless actor_kind may perform act.\"\"\"\n54|    allowed = _PERMITTED.get(act)\n55|    if allowed is None:\n56|        raise AuthorityViolation(\n57|            \"unknown authoritative act %r; no actor may perform it\" % act\n58|        )\n59|    if actor_kind not in allowed:\n60|        raise AuthorityViolation(\n61|            \"actor kind %r may not perform %r (permitted: %s)\"\n62|            % (actor_kind, act, \", \".join(sorted(allowed)))\n63|        )\n64|\n65|\n66|def known_acts() -> FrozenSet[str]:\n67|    return frozenset(_PERMITTED)\n68|", "total_lines": 67, "file_size": 2494, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

The body is a snapshot from filing time; the newest comments carry the live state: partial fixes already merged, new root-cause analyses, maintainer decisions, or questions directed at you that change the task. Also read repository instructions (`AGENTS.md`, contribution docs) with `read_file`. Done when the currently requested behavior, non-goals, and any unanswered thread questions are known.\n\n### 2. Sweep for existing and duplicate work\n\nBefore writing anything, run `gh pr list --search \"#<N>\" --state all` plus at least two keyword/synonym variants of the symptom (`gh pr list --search \"<subsystem> <symptom>\" --state open`). Popular issues attract multiple independent fixes; building a duplicate wastes the work and the credit. Also check whether a recent commit already fixed it: `git log --oneline -20 -- <relevant files>`. Done when you know every open PR and recent commit touching this issue, or that none exist.\n\n### 3. Validate the premise against current code — and against design intent\n\nReproduce the bug or demonstrate the missing behavior on the current default branch with a failing test or fixture, using `search_files` and `read_file` to trace the reported path. Then check the second question: is the \"bug\" actually deliberate design? Run `git log -p -S \"<symbol>\"` on the code the issue wants changed and read the original commit's intent — a missing link or restriction is often the feature. Challenge stale or flawed issue prose instead of implementing it blindly. Done when the root cause or feature gap is demonstrated in current code AND the change doesn't fight an intentional design.\n\n### 4. Define acceptance and risk\n\nList acceptance criteria, interfaces, migrations/state changes, compatibility, security/privacy, rollout, and rollback. Map every criterion to a test or explicit verification. Done when review has a finite contract.\n\n### 5. Implement the smallest complete change — and fix the class\n\nWork on an isolated branch or worktree, loading `systematic-debugging` or `test-driven-development` when the bug class calls for them. Add regression tests first, then implement. When the fix is in hand, `search_files` for the same bug shape at sibling call sites and fix the whole class in this PR — an incomplete fix that leaves known siblings broken is worse than none. Every changed line must trace to the issue; no drive-by cleanup. Done when targeted tests pass, the original failure no longer reproduces, and sibling sites are fixed or explicitly ruled out.\n\n### 6. Prove the regression test bites (sabotage run)\n\nTemporarily restore the old behavior of the exact function under test, run the new test, and confirm it FAILS; then restore the fix and confirm it passes. A regression test that passes with and without the fix proves nothing. Done when the test demonstrably fails on pre-fix code.\n\n### 7. Run repository quality gates, then open the PR immediately\n\nRun the formatter, lint, typecheck, and the repo's canonical test entrypoint on affected areas; use `requesting-code-review` on the diff. Then push and open the PR right away — the PR is what dispatches CI, and CI latency is the long pole; do not sit on finished work. Load `github-pr-workflow` for PR mechanics: conventional branch/commit, body linking the issue with problem, approach, tests, risk, and exclusions. Read the PR back and verify head SHA, base, title, and files. Done when the PR exists with the intended diff and CI is running.\n\n### 8. Shepherd CI honestly and close the loop\n\nInspect live checks and failure logs via `gh pr checks` / `gh run view --log-failed`. Distinguish failures introduced by your diff from pre-existing baseline or infrastructure failures — reproduce on the default branch when unsure, and rerun once only for genuine infra flakes. Never say \"green,\" \"merged,\" or \"released\" without live evidence of that exact state. When the PR lands, comment on the issue with the PR link and a one-line explanation so the reporter gets a traceable resolution. Done when CI state, remaining blockers, and the issue thread all reflect reality.\n\n## Pitfalls\n\n- Coding before reading issue comments, sweeping for duplicate PRs, or reading current code.\n- \"Fixing\" behavior that the original commit shows is intentional design.\n- Fixing a symptom at one call site while sibling sites keep the same bug.\n- Shipping a regression test that also passes without the fix.\n- Opening a PR with unrun tests or unrelated formatting churn.\n- Claiming the issue is delivered because a PR exists.\n\n## Verification\n\n- [ ] Full issue thread read; newest comment state reflected in the plan.\n- [ ] Duplicate-PR sweep run with issue number + 2 keyword variants.\n- [ ] Premise reproduced on current code; design intent checked via git history.\n- [ ] Regression test proven to fail without the fix.\n- [ ] Sibling call sites fixed or explicitly ruled out.\n- [ ] Every changed line traces to the issue.\n- [ ] CI state reported from live evidence only; issue commented with the PR link.\n", "path": "github/github-issue-to-pr/SKILL.md", "skill_dir": "/Users/knowurknot/.hermes/skills/github/github-issue-to-pr", "org_provenance": null, "linked_files": null, "usage_hint": null, "required_environment_variables": [], "required_commands": [], "missing_required_environment_variables": [], "missing_credential_files": [], "missing_required_commands": [], "setup_needed": false, "setup_skipped": false, "readiness_status": "available", "_source_path": "/Users/knowurknot/.hermes/skills/github/github-issue-to-pr/SKILL.md", "metadata": {"hermes": {"tags": ["GitHub", "Issues", "Coding", "Pull-Requests", "CI"], "related_skills": ["github-issues", "github-pr-workflow", "systematic-debugging", "test-driven-development", "requesting-code-review"]}}}

# AGENTS.md — CAPT Manual Hardening Rules

These instructions apply to every human, AI agent, scanner, reviewer, and remediation workflow using this repository.

## 1. Mission boundary

The mission is to finish CAPT Core v0.5 manually and defensibly. Do not expand into deferred architecture unless a release-blocking defect requires it.

Do not build:

- a CRP runtime;
- distributed schedulers;
- cloud control planes;
- central user accounts;
- new cognitive modules;
- speculative multi-agent orchestration;
- broad package splits;
- a wholesale universal record-envelope migration.

## 2. Repository boundary

This repository contains instructions and evidence formats only. CAPT source changes belong in the actual CAPT repository on a dedicated hardening branch.

Never copy secrets, private runtime state, `.capt_state/`, credentials, tokens, or user data into this repository.

## 3. State before action

Before every work session, capture:

```text
repository
branch
HEAD SHA
git status --short
staged changes
unstaged changes
untracked files
tool versions
Python version
operating system
```

Treat the worktree as unsafe to modify until unexpected changes are classified.

## 4. Evidence-first rule

Every security or release claim must identify:

- exact subject;
- exact SHA or artifact digest;
- state and scope;
- command or method;
- tool and version;
- input;
- output;
- timestamp;
- limitations;
- reviewer or agent identity.

No agent may use its own unsupported assertion as both discovery evidence and validation evidence.

## 5. Separation of duties

The minimum finding pipeline is:

```text
Discovery Agent
→ Independent Validator
→ Impact Tracer
→ Remediation Agent
→ Regression Verifier
→ Release Decision
```

The same agent may assist more than one stage only when every stage produces independently reproducible artifacts and another agent or human reviews the disposition.

## 6. Candidate findings are not findings

Scanner output is a candidate observation. It becomes a validated finding only after:

1. the affected code and path are confirmed;
2. reachability is established;
3. attacker prerequisites are stated;
4. the trust-boundary crossing is identified;
5. impact is demonstrated or tightly reasoned;
6. false-positive explanations are considered;
7. evidence is preserved.

## 7. Minimal remediation

Security fixes must:

- be the smallest change that closes the validated weakness;
- preserve compatibility unless a breaking change is explicitly approved;
- add a regression test;
- avoid unrelated refactors;
- fail closed;
- preserve local-first behavior;
- preserve provenance and invalidation semantics;
- avoid introducing network access or new dependencies without approval.

## 8. Required validation after every fix

Run, at minimum:

- focused regression test;
- related subsystem tests;
- semantic release validation;
- architecture validation;
- workspace validation;
- full test suite before release closure.

## 9. Security claims

Never write:

- “secure” without scope;
- “fully scanned” when coverage is partial;
- “ISO compliant” or “SOC 2 compliant” merely because CAPT emits evidence;
- “zero network” unless imports and advertised profiles were tested;
- “release ready” without exact-SHA artifacts and a sealed report.

Preferred language:

- “No validated Critical or High findings were identified within the documented scope at SHA …”
- “Designed to support evidence collection for …”
- “Local-first by default; optional integrations are separately gated.”

## 10. Codex Security usage constraint

Treat repository-wide Codex deep scans as high-cost, non-deterministic operational dependencies. A user-reported run consumed approximately 74% of the remaining weekly allowance on a $20 membership and failed during discovery with no canonical report.

Future policy:

- never start a deep scan before the candidate is stable;
- preserve artifacts from every attempt;
- set explicit budget and stop conditions;
- use deterministic tools and manual review first;
- never make Codex Security the sole release gate;
- use it, when available, as independent corroboration.

This is an observed project constraint, not a universal claim about all accounts or future product behavior.

## 11. Stop conditions

Stop and escalate when:

- the worktree contains unexplained changes;
- a tool attempts to alter user-owned state;
- a finding cannot be independently reproduced;
- a proposed fix broadens authority or networking;
- evidence refers to a superseded SHA;
- a Critical or High finding remains unresolved;
- the release documents disagree;
- the final wheel and sdist differ from advertised capabilities.

## 12. Final decision vocabulary

Use exactly one:

```text
READY FOR OWNER AUTHORIZATION
```

or

```text
NOT READY — BLOCKERS REMAIN
```

Agents must not tag, publish, merge, or release without explicit owner authorization.
